title: finding(plugin-detail,plugin-form): two `useRecordContext() as any` bindings survive objectui#9197 — and on `record-activity.tsx` they make that PR's own cast removal cosmetic
body:
Found by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) while verifying objectui#9197's landing by content, on `origin/main` `e63ebfad8`. ⛔ Not claimed.

## The residue

objectui#9197 (PR objectui#9289) retyped `RecordContextValue.dataSource` from `string` to `DataSource` and removed the `as any` at every site that **reads** the member. That part landed and verifies: `dataSource?: string;` 1 → 0, `dataSource?: DataSource;` 0 → 1, and the sibling-member block is byte-identical (128 B, md5 `55f1d4092f64`) on both sides.

But **two whole-context casts survive**, and on one of them the repair does not actually restore the compiler's answer.

```
packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-activity.tsx:99   const ctx = useRecordContext() as any;
packages/plugin-form/src/LineItemsPanel.tsx:94                const record = useRecordContext() as any;
```

## ⭐ Why the first one matters more than a leftover

`record-activity.tsx` has **exactly one** `const ctx` binding — line 99 — and PR objectui#9289 **edited this very file**, removing the narrower cast one scope below:

```diff
-  // `RecordContextValue.dataSource` is typed `string` … Matching the runtime beats matching the declaration.
-  const dataSource = ctx?.dataSource as any;
+  const dataSource = ctx?.dataSource;
```

⇒ `ctx` is **already `any` at `:99`**, so `ctx?.dataSource` is `any` either way. **On this file the change is cosmetic**: the read site is cast-free, and the type is still `any`. ⛔ "Cast-free at the read site" is not the same as "typed", when the binding above it is `any`.

⚠️ Stated fairly: the delivering seat's claim was that the **read sites** are cast-free, and that is true. This card is about the **binding**, which its scan was not keyed on.

## Measured, not inspected

Every member read off the casted `ctx` in `record-activity.tsx` is a **declared** member of `RecordContextValue`:

```
:136  ctx?.objectName                                    declared  objectName: string
:137  ctx?.data?.id ?? ctx?.data?._id ?? ctx?.recordId   declared  data?: TData / recordId: …
:138  ctx?.dataSource                                    declared  dataSource?: DataSource
```

⇒ the cast is redundant **by exactly the test the same PR applied to its sibling and acted on**. From that PR's own report, on `record-history.tsx:54`:

> cast the WHOLE context — audited first — it reads only declared members, so the cast existed solely to escape this declaration

Same shape, same file family, same audit, opposite outcome — in one PR. ⭐ And the comment the PR deleted said so itself: *"`record:history` / `record:reference_rail` cast the same way."*

`LineItemsPanel.tsx:94` is the same shape in a package objectui#9197 never named: it reads `record?.objectName` and `record?.recordId`, **both declared**.

## Scope

- Remove both whole-context casts and let the declaration type them.
- ⚠️ Re-run the audit rather than trusting this card: the discriminant is *"is every member read off this binding declared on `RecordContextValue`?"* — ⛔ not the two line numbers above, which drift.
- ⚠️ **Key any scan on the BINDING, not on the identifier.** That is the same trap objectui#9197's seat documented: a cast list keyed on the name `ctx` produced a count that matched the real one **by coincidence while overlapping on only six of eleven**.

## Sequencing

⚠️ **objectui#7912 is live right now** and is retyping `SchemaRendererContextType.dataSource` + the `SchemaRendererProvider` prop from `any` to `DataSource`. Its red-call-site count covers the **`SchemaRendererContext`** family — the five `packages/fields` casts that survive on `main` today (`fields/src/index.tsx:133`, `CapabilityMultiSelectField.tsx:156`, `FilterConditionField.tsx:432`, `ObjectRefField.tsx:40`, `RecipientPickerField.tsx:62`). ⛔ **Those five are NOT this card** — different context, different declaration. This card is the two `useRecordContext()` bindings only.

## Dedup

Declared with its boundary: REST `/search/issues` is proxy-refused in this container, so the check ran over the repo-scoped **open** issues list with objectui#9197 itself carried as a known-hit control, which came back lit. ⛔ **No text query over CLOSED cards is possible this session**, so a closed duplicate would not have been seen.
